title: Set 65

sentences.ko: 점심 들고 앉아서 영상 하나 틀었는데, 그게 저절로 다음 편으로 넘어가는 거야. 그걸 한 번도 안 껐어. 그렇게 쉬는 시간이 통째로 날아갔는데, 내가 뭘 봤는지 말도 못 하겠어. 이제 오늘 밤 여덟 시까지 내 시간이라곤 1분도 없어.
sentences.text: I sat down with my lunch and put one video on, and then it just rolls into the next one by itself, and I never stopped it. So there goes my whole break, and I couldn't even tell you what I watched. Now I'm not getting a minute to myself until eight tonight.

alts.text: So I've got my lunch, I put one video on, and the thing just keeps rolling into the next one by itself, and I never turned it off. There goes my whole break, and I couldn't even tell you what I watched. Now I don't get a minute to myself till eight tonight.

I sat down to eat my lunch and started one video, and it simply continued into the next one automatically, and I never stopped it. My entire break is gone, and I could not tell you what I watched. Now I will not have a moment to myself until eight this evening.

sentences.note: **there goes my whole break** 는 쉬는 시간이 그렇게 다 날아갔다고 아쉬워할 때 쓰는 말입니다. **a minute to myself** 는 오롯이 나만 쓰는 시간을 뜻합니다.
sentences.situation: 유튜브 보다가 시간 다 날린 얘기

sentences.ko: 그 드라마 처음 두 시즌은 정말 좋아해서 다들 보라고 하고 다녔어. 그래서 지금은 좀 내 책임 같기도 해. 그런데 그 시즌들 쓴 작가들이 나갔고, 티가 나. 이제는 나오는 사람마다 속으로 생각하는 걸 그대로 소리 내서 말하거든. 그런데도 나는 아직 보고 있고, 그러니까 나도 문제의 일부인 셈이지.
sentences.text: I loved that show the first two seasons, and I told everybody to watch it, so I feel a little responsible now. But the people who wrote those seasons left, and you can tell, because now everybody on it just says exactly what they're thinking out loud. And I'm still watching, which I know makes me part of the problem.

alts.text: First two seasons of that show, I loved it, and I told everybody to watch it, so I kinda feel responsible now. But the writers from those seasons are gone, and you can tell, cause now everybody on it just says whatever they're thinking right out loud. And I'm still watching, which I know makes me part of the problem.

I greatly enjoyed that show for its first two seasons, and I recommended it to everyone, so I feel somewhat responsible now. However, the writers of those seasons left, and it is apparent, because now every character states exactly what they are thinking aloud. And I am still watching, which I am aware makes me part of the problem.

sentences.note: **you can tell** 은 티가 난다, 딱 봐도 알겠다는 뜻입니다. **makes me part of the problem** 은 나도 그 문제에 한몫하고 있다는 말입니다.

sentences.ko: 그 사람이 물어보면, 내 기차가 역 사이에 20분 서 있었던 거야, 알았지? 사실은 내가 알람을 하루의 반대쪽 끝에 맞춰 놨거든. 아침 여섯 시 반이 아니라 저녁 여섯 시 반으로. 그 얘기를 저 안에서 입 밖에 낼 수는 없어. 그러니까 뭘 더 보태지 말고, 그냥 기차 때문이었다고만 해.
sentences.text: If she asks, my train sat between stations for twenty minutes, alright? Because what actually happened is I set the alarm for the wrong end of the day, six thirty at night instead of the morning, and I'm not saying that out loud in there. So don't add anything to it, just say it was the train.

alts.text: The train sat between stations for twenty minutes, that's the story if she asks, alright? Cause what really happened is I set the alarm for the wrong end of the day, six thirty at night instead of the morning, and I'm not saying that out loud in there. So don't add anything to it, just say it was the train.

If she asks, my train remained between stations for twenty minutes, agreed? Because what actually happened is that I set the alarm for the wrong end of the day, six thirty in the evening rather than the morning, and I am not going to say that aloud in there. So please do not add anything to it. Simply say that it was the train.

sentences.note: **the wrong end of the day** 는 아침과 저녁을 거꾸로 잡았다는 말입니다. **don't add anything to it** 는 거기에 말을 더 보태지 말라는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 자, 그동안 얘기 좀 해 줘. 내가 마지막으로 들은 건 네가 가을에 학교로 돌아갈지 아직 정하는 중이라는 거였는데, 그게 2월쯤이었나? 그 사이에 네 여동생 결혼식도 있었고. 어디서부터 시작해도 돼. 나 안 급해.
sentences.text: Okay, catch me up, because the last thing I heard you were still deciding whether to go back to school in the fall, and that was like February? And your sister was getting married somewhere in there too. Start wherever you want, I'm not in a hurry.

alts.text: Alright, fill me in, cause last I knew you were still figuring out whether to go back to school in the fall, and that was what, February? And your sister was getting married somewhere in there too. Start wherever you want, I'm not in a rush.

Please bring me up to date, because the last I heard, you were still deciding whether to return to school in the fall, and that was around February? And your sister was getting married somewhere in that period as well. Begin wherever you like. I am not in any hurry.

sentences.note: **catch me up** 은 그동안 있었던 일을 나에게 알려 달라는 말입니다. **somewhere in there** 는 그 기간 어디쯤이라는 뜻입니다.

sentences.ko: 지난달 전기 요금이 220달러 나왔어. 우리가 뭘 다르게 한 것도 없거든. 같은 집에, 둘이 사는 것도 그대로고. 그래서 전화했더니 직원이 6월에 요금이 올랐다는 말만 하고는 우리 사용량 설명을 한 페이지 통째로 읽어 주더라. 그러고는 매달 같은 금액씩 내는 요금제 설명 들어 보겠냐고 물어. 그건 덜 내는 게 아니잖아. 그냥 같은 돈을 나눠서 내는 거지.
sentences.text: My electric bill was two hundred and twenty dollars last month, and we haven't done a thing different, same house, same two of us. So I called them, and the guy just tells me rates went up in June and reads me this whole page about my usage. Then he asks if I want to hear about the budget plan, and that's not paying less, that's just paying the same money spread out.

alts.text: Two hundred and twenty dollars, that's what my electric bill was last month, and we haven't changed a thing, same house, same two of us. So I call them, and the guy just goes rates went up in June and reads me this whole page about my usage. Then he asks if I wanna hear about the budget plan, and that's not paying less, that's just paying the same money spread out.

My electricity bill was two hundred and twenty dollars last month, and we have not done anything differently, the same house and the same two of us. I called them, and the representative simply told me that rates increased in June and read me an entire page regarding my usage. He then asked whether I would like to hear about the budget plan, which is not paying less. It is merely paying the same amount spread out.

sentences.note: **rates went up** 은 요금이 올랐다는 뜻입니다. **spread out** 은 같은 금액을 여러 달에 나눠 낸다는 말입니다.

reviewed: 5번 formal 의 "I therefore telephoned them" 은 요즘 미국 영어에서 안 쓰는 낡은 말이라 "I called them" 으로 고쳤습니다. 격식은 나머지 문장에서 이미 지켜집니다.
5번 한국어 "예산 요금제" 는 budget plan 을 글자대로 옮긴 번역투였습니다. 실제 제도가 무엇인지 풀어서 "매달 같은 금액씩 내는 요금제" 로 바꿨습니다.
5번 한국어 "우리가 달라지게 한 건 하나도 없거든" 이 어색해서 "우리가 뭘 다르게 한 것도 없거든" 으로 고쳤습니다.
1번 한국어 "나한테 쓸 시간이 1분도 없어" 를 "내 시간이라곤 1분도 없어" 로 다듬었습니다. a minute to myself 의 뜻은 그대로입니다.
4번 한국어 "네 여동생 결혼도 있었고" 를 "결혼식도" 로 고쳤습니다 — 한국어에서는 결혼식이라고 말합니다.
영어(text)는 소리내어 읽는 단계에서 이미 확정된 것이라 한 글자도 손대지 않았습니다. 관용구(there goes my whole break, the wrong end of the day, catch me up, rates went up)는 모두 제자리에 쓰였고, note 가 짚은 표현도 전부 문장 안에 실제로 있습니다.
